changes.text: Fixed the redesign's navigation and dashboard. On a wide screen there is one navigation again, the labelled list; the icon rail only stands in for it on a tablet. The dashboard now uses the whole screen: the three fact cards on top, below them the machines (host, state, role, address, Talos version) and, beside them, every cluster with its nodes and certificate and the latest audit records.
On a phone the three fact cards sit in one row, and the Kubernetes sections are one row that scrolls sideways (the open one stays in view) instead of three rows.

The interface is the 2026 redesign: on a desk and a tablet the navigation is an icon rail (Dashboard, Clusters, Host, Jobs, Settings) with the full list as a labelled column beside it, on a phone the five sit as a bottom tab bar with icons and labels. The dashboard shows the fleet as cards with one big number each -- clusters, machines, the instance's own state -- instead of stacked reports. Logo, colours and every rule the shell carries (the Host mark, the audit chain warning, the 44px phone targets) are unchanged.
Fixed: the navigation's name and tagline fit on one line each. The bar is a little wider (240 px); the tagline had broken onto two lines and the name could run past the edge.
Releases are built for the Raspberry Pi 5 only for now (linux/arm64). The archives for amd64, macOS and Windows are gone, for the daemon and for holzkubectl; a Pi updating itself notices nothing.

The interface takes the new brand colour. The accent is Glut instead of brass: buttons, the selected navigation entry, focus rings, the Alpha badge and the first line of every chart. In the light theme, text and borders in that colour use a darker Glut, so they keep the contrast they had. Nothing else changes.

New Host page: the machine holzkube-manager runs on — device, service, live CPU, memory, filesystems, temperatures and network, with history over 1 h, 6 h and 24 h, a warning that names its reason, and a tile on the wall. What the service's hardening hides is shown as "not readable", never as 0.

Five host actions on /host: check for updates (installs nothing), check for updates and install, restart the service, restart the host, shut it down. Each needs the operator role, a fresh re-authentication and the typed host name, and is in the audit log. holzkube-manager never does them itself: a small root-owned helper from deploy/ carries them out, and the page says what to install while it is missing or too old.

The hourly update now ships as units in deploy/ (holzkube-manager-update.service and .timer, plus a unit for the daemon itself). The update script checks the host before it installs, rolls back when the restart fails, and never runs twice at once. Your hand-made units keep working; deploy/HOST-HELPER.md says how to switch to the shipped ones.
On a phone every control is at least 44 px, also inside menus and dialogs; the build fails when one is smaller. Nothing changes above tablet width.

Settings → Accounts can unlink an account from single sign-on, so you can move to another identity provider. Unlinking ends the sessions that came in through that link; the next single sign-on from the local network links the new provider and is recorded in the audit log. Service accounts no longer block linking, and an address that only accepts single sign-on no longer answers "setup required" when there is more than one account.

Not yet run on real hardware: the host helper, the shipped update units under their sandbox, and the phone hand test. Install the helper per deploy/HOST-HELPER.md and start with Check for updates, which changes nothing.

Kubernetes upgrades rebuilt. The upgrade now runs in the order talosctl upgrade-k8s uses: it pulls every image onto every node first, then moves kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler node by node, waiting until each node reports the pod ready on its new image, then kube-proxy (its DaemonSet included, with a rollout wait), and the kubelets last.

Fixed: a Kubernetes upgrade would have replaced a node's whole configuration with its few image lines, and a real node refuses that, so every run would have stopped at its first node. Each change now merges into the configuration the node has, in the shape it keeps it (Talos v1.14 documents or the older fields).
The Kubernetes upgrade is tested end to end against the simulator, not yet against a real cluster. Take an etcd snapshot before you run it.
The update script finds prerelease builds and, after a healthy update, replaces itself from the release archive. A host running the script from before v0.0.1 needs the new one installed once by hand.

A fresh start at 0.0.1. holzkube-manager is alpha software under heavy development: any release can change or break features, the API and the data directory's format. Keep a backup of the data directory and read these notes before updating. Everything below is what this first alpha already does.

Clusters and nodes: adopt an existing Talos cluster from its talosconfig or provision a new one. The manager follows the cluster's own membership, so a node that joins or leaves shows up by itself, and every page reads live from the cluster when you open it.
Live hardware per node: load overall and per core, memory, disks, network, temperatures and fans, with the last 24 hours kept across restarts.
Apps: everything that runs on Kubernetes, grouped by what was installed, with its CPU and memory now and over the day, and a page per app with its pods, services and events.
Kubernetes: workloads, pods and why one is broken, events, storage, networking, quotas, who may do what, cordon and drain, applying a manifest and running a command in a container.
Power for a cluster, a node or an app: stop, force stop, start, disable, enable, restart and force restart. Start wakes a switched-off node by Wake-on-LAN.
Talos upgrades built from Image Factory schematics, SecureBoot, disk encryption, etcd snapshots and restore, and certificate renewal.
A wall for a screen in the office: every node and workload as a tile, how full the cluster is, the day's load and the latest warnings.

A local account and single sign-on, roles, a password prompt before anything destructive, a hash-chained audit log and a dry-run mode. holzkubectl on the command line, Prometheus metrics and a support bundle.
A mark of its own: annual rings in a hexagon, as the tab icon, in the sidebar and on a phone's home screen.
